validation.scope: All eight tresillo multipliers for literal bank1/pattern2 and the drum-bank 64-step boundary. Full64-cell paint/repaint, two complete MIDI cycles plus closing onset and every inter-onset gap including wraps. All five drum banks and four numeric masks at selected literal patterns, including empty-bank silence.
validation.limitations: Selected bank/pattern fixtures do not cover all fader values, all combinations or running edits. Full manual and release remain incomplete.
validation.initial_porting_failure: Four native attempts failed on a nonexistent driver send method before rhythm assertions; corrected to public action API and retained in local tresillo-porting-error evidence.
validation.fix: Apply previously isolated0004 candidate: wrap bit index at stored pattern length before byte lookup. Larger3m tresillo segments no longer read nil past16-bit drum data. Existing drum output is independently checked unchanged.

bugs.remaining: Wrap, masks, merges and restoration remain campaign obligations; not full length-family certification.

bugs.historical_case: M-LEN-003 before separating distinct-pitch duration coverage
bugs.failure: Required stop drain times out: repeated pitch Note Ons have missing matching Note Offs.

bugs.finding: First two-step note at90 BPM is328611113ns rather than333333333.333ns; subsequent durations agree within1ns. Generic native absolute-sync phase probe agrees with independent120BPM expectations. Immediate lattice pulse followed by absolute96PPQN sync is the suspected source. Do not waive or widen tolerance.
bugs.remaining: Five restart phase edges now pass controlled and real time. Clock-source transitions, fresh final-source3-repeat matrix and M5/P5 remain required. Historical intermittent timing failures are retained separately from the corrected first-pulse phase regression.

bugs.finding: Clearing a route removes its menu depth but leaves the parameter modulation cache active. All notes remain127 rather than restoring60/62/64/65.

Rebinding depth1.00 to macro1 held at1 leaves original pitches60/62/64/65 instead of127. set_depth omitted the depth argument to nilmul. Baseline includes the earlier clear-cache fix to isolate this second defect.

Continuous25ms pulse schedule misses its next target while synchronous grid/snapshot actions complete. Real-time test fails before source selection; no Mosaic defect established. Do not shift the input clock timeline to obtain a pass.

A pre-grid snapshot preceded audible onset by26.907ms and overcounted elapsed ticks. RT now uses the emitted onset and native applied-control acknowledgement, retaining the10ms bound. No Mosaic production defect established.

bugs.summary: Shift press to stop accepted K3, not the documented shift (K1), as the short-press stop modifier.

With Elektron program changes on, m_clock announces the next song slot when current_step == global_pattern_length - 1, before the slot switch. Global length 4 announces each transition once, two steps ahead (M-OPT-ELEK-001 passes). Length 2: at Play the current-slot change is followed at the same instant by the next-slot change, before slot 1 sounds, and each later announcement coincides with the boundary it names. Length 1: no transition is announced.

bugs.source_observation: step.process_elektron_program_change sends one change per Elektron-device channel through devices[1].midi_device; multi-port and duplicate behaviour are not yet exercised.

bugs.summary: Mapped relative increases were ignored after boot until a decrease fired, because mapping parameters defaulted to 1.
One device config entry without an id aborted Mosaic initialisation.
A slot selected while song mode was off stayed queued and redirected the first transition after song mode was re-enabled.
A live-recorded note held across a song transition was stored in the slot selected at release instead of the slot and step active at its first press.
After the bounded memory history wrapped, a new action recorded after moving back was stored in the wrong slot, so undoing it reverted a different action.
After about 100 saves of the playing scale in one session, pressing Play raised a Lua error in the quantiser cache cleanup and stopped the sequencer.
A step lock on an nb (norns-parameter) device parameter such as Doubledecker Shape 1 raised a Lua error at Play and stopped the sequencer.
After a save and reload, channel and step length masks of 1/24, 1/12, 1/6, 1/3, 2/3 or 5/6 were shown as X on the Note Masks page.
With one long slide running, busy slides on other parameters stopped moving after about 1000 replacements and only jumped between lock values until the long slide ended.
After + New, the Memory page still showed the previous project's history and E3 could replay those actions onto the new project.
With Elektron program changes on, an Elektron device on a MIDI port other than channel 1's never received program changes, and channel 1's port received duplicates.
After a few tooltips, the idle-autosave Autosaved tooltip stayed on screen until another tooltip replaced it.
A song slot or global length queued during playback survived Stop invisibly and took effect at the first boundary of the next Play.
Copying a song slot erased the source instead when the source key was released before the destination key.

A complete pattern-note tap 30 ms before a song boundary was heard one pass late on channel 16 because the next slot rebuild cancelled the committed edit rebuild. Per-song debouncing preserves both slot sweeps while retaining same-slot coalescing.
bugs.note: Qualified baseline: three real-time and three controlled runs failed with both callbacks completed before the boundary. Candidate: three fresh real-time runs and three normalized controlled repeats pass. The focused scheduler unit fails on unfixed 2eba587 and covers early/late channels, repeated same-slot edits, simultaneous other-slot work and song isolation.

bugs.summary: With a step held, a fixed-channel mask map edited that channel's step masks from the selected channel's value, outside memory.
The Digitakt 2 configuration was named "Digitakt".
Syntakt Sustain and Sostenuto could not be set.
Redo of an encoder-made held-step lock silenced the step until the next pattern rebuild.

A paint press within the ~60 ms it takes the prime job to rebuild the paint pattern (18 scheduler ticks) saves a partial pattern and the job then re-shows the preview; the in-case control (paint after the preview settles) paints the full exclusive-or. README 424-428. Human decision 2026-09-11: fix now. Fixed (S16): Paint builds and saves the complete primed pattern, and a job overtaken by Paint or Cancel no longer re-shows the preview.

After a Note Off that never arrives (MIDI port disconnected while a key and a step are held), later single-key entries on that step add chord voices (72, then 72+76, then 72+76+79) instead of replacing the note; Stop and Panic do not clear it (they reset an unused module variable). Reproduced by probe_chord.py in the controlled lane (variants none, stop, panic). README 239 does not say which reset is intended. Human decision 2026-09-11: Stop resets keyboard chord state; fixed (M-KEYBOARD-STOP-001).
Note Dashboard showed Vel -1 and Len -1.0 after a grid channel select; now X like the Note cell (S50)
Stepping memory back now restores the whole prior step state: unrelated fields, earlier chords and other trig-lock parameters no longer leak through an undo (S42-S44)
Chd3 up-then-down on a held step now sounds the selected chord note and is one memory action, like the other chord handlers (S25)
A mapped CC on MIDI channels 2-16 switched the channel editor page and never returned; the return now works on every channel (S10)
A repeated Note On for a held key (merged keyboards) replaced its release record and left one output note stuck; each onset now keeps its own release (S8)
The same key held from two MIDI inputs shared one chord slot, so the first release ended the chord early; chord lengths now run to the final release (S9, S38)
With record armed, holding a page or menu key dropped live-recorded notes and committed a length-only mask; such holds now record normally (S32)
One device config file that could not be opened (for example a broken symlink in the config folder) stopped Mosaic from starting, with no devices loaded; it is now skipped and the other configs load.
A Chord Accel Mod trig lock on a channel playing an n.b. device raised a Lua error at the locked step during playback; the lock is now handled by the sequencer like the other chord parameters.

Switching a channel from a MIDI device to an n.b. device without params (for example Jf Kit) left the old device's parameters in the channel's norns params menu, still sending MIDI; they are now cleared.
A reset in the middle of a channel step ran the restarted first step straight/unrounded: swing pairs shifted after a song transition, fractional clocks and their slides off by a pulse (S41, S53)
Memory undo of a step-slid lock left that parameter's step slide set when another lock remained on the step, so the outline stayed and a later lock there slid without K3 (S34).
Trig Locks dials show X at Off when Off lies below the range (off -1, min 0) and for MIDI device params without off_value (default -1), instead of an empty or half bar and a 0/-1 read-out

Note Dashboard chord slots show the chord voices as sent (MIDI 0 and clamped voices below 0 show C-2) and X for slots that never played, instead of keeping the previous name, showing unclamped names, or C-2 on a fresh dashboard
A held pattern-row key made mask handlers record step -30 or, pressed first, turned a held-step edit into a channel-wide one; keys outside rows 4-7 are now ignored (S27)

Grid disconnect kept held keys, their long-press timers and gesture state; disconnect now clears them (S29, defensive, no behaviour reproduction by decision). No behaviour reproduction exists, by decision: an emulator probe showed no user-visible effect; the human decided on 2026-09-11 to fix defensively, with Lua units that fail before the fix as the regression.
Redo-all (K3) kept only the later chord edit on a step; chord voices now merge per voice (S57)
A severe external-clock callback backlog could replay stale notes after native MIDI Stop; catch-up now yields so queued transport preempts stale musical work.
Preserve the correct undo floor after bounded memory history wraps.
On note/velocity editor step pages 2-4 the chosen pattern's top-row active LED did not flicker; it now does, as on page 1 (S18)
An unset chord mask turned once showed X (up) or -6th (down); it now starts from X: 2nd up, -7th down (S26)

S24 probe (M-MASK-OFF-001, both lanes): a channel velocity mask turned back to X plays as unset, but held-step masks turned back to X do not. Step 2's trig mask turned N then back to X stays silent (the handler stores trig -1 as a step lock, and pattern.lua applies any step trig lock, so -1 is not 1 and the step never plays). Step 3's velocity lock 50 turned back to X keeps velocity 50 (the -1 portion fails memory's validate_velocity, so the release commits nothing). Both survive an autosave restart; one Memory-page step back after the restart left the phrase unchanged (observation). README 570/597: a step without a mask lock uses the channel/pattern value. The fix (nil for X, or -1 treated as unset, per field; chord masks must keep -1 as '-7th') needs a human decision.
